newsitem.title: USA: Maytag CEO backs FY 97 EPS estimate.
newsitem.headline: Maytag CEO backs FY 97 EPS estimate.

text.p: Maytag Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Leonard Hadley said he was comfortable with Wall Street analysts' consensus earnings per share estimates of $1.81 for 1997.
Speaking to Reuters after the company unveiled its new horizontal-axis washing machine in New York City, he said "I am comfortable with what analysts have."

Hadley also said that the company sees the last half of the year as being much stronger than the first half because of all the startup costs associated with the introduction of new products. "The profit benefit will be in the back end of the year when they're in the marketplace," he said.
"The $1.81 would be better than that if we didn't have the negative of the first two quarters," he added.

Maytag has been refocusing its attention on the U.S. market, launching several new products in 1997, including a new line of refrigerators and the Neptune horizontal-axis washing machine unveiled on Thursday.
The company plans to introduce a new design of its Hoover upright floor cleaner in the second half of the year.
According to the company, the Neptune washer, a front-load machine with no agitator, cleans and treats clothes better than conventional machines and considerably reduces both water and energy usage.
These features come at a price: the Neptune line, which is expected to debut in retail stores by mid-year, will be priced at around $999 for the washer and $499 for the accompanying dryer.
Hadley told Reuters that the company was positioning the appliances at the top end on the grounds that "we see this industry as being a two-platform industry indefinitely going forward."

He said the company expected a significant market for this line going into the future and added that cost savings from lower energy and water use, as well as those arising from less wear and tear on clothes, would draw in customers.
According to Lawrence Horan, an analyst at Prudential Securities, "There is a huge debate as to whether people will accept them (horizontal-axis washers) or not." He said they
were popular in Europe but had not caught on in the U.S.
Hadley agreed, but said that the Neptune line differentiated itself from European machines in terms of speed, capacity and convenience.

Susan Gallagher, an analyst at NatWest Securities, said "We think they'll have a good 1997," but added that NatWest was keeping its hold rating on the stock until it had a better sense of how a couple of factors would play out.

The first is the success of the new refrigerator line, on which the company spent $180 million and which will be shipped to dealers in April. The second, Gallagher said, was the issue of Amana, Raytheon Co's appliance division, which is said to be up for sale. "We're waiting to see who buys it," she said, and what the consequent impact would be on Maytag.
